claims.statement: For ordinary trees T and p with x(T)+2<=p, 3p<2alpha(T)+1, and |T|=2p+2, the complete sum over original leaves satisfying Delta_p(T-v)<0 of Delta_(p-1)(T-{v,s_v})-Delta_(p-1)(T-N_T[s_v]) is nonpositive.
claims.scope: Exact registered first-order shell; original leaves remain distinct tags and use their original supports, neighborhoods, and the fixed strict favorable selector.
claims.reason: The ordered-root decomposition bounds all positive terms by first-root and first-isolate lower counts, but the necessary selector-conditioned global compensation inequality (Comp) is not proved, and no complete-sum counterexample is supplied.

claims.statement: For each eligible shell leaf tag with nonempty H_v, the marked count difference q_(k+1)-q_k decomposes by ordered component marks as sum_i(i_k(J_i)-i_(k-1)(J_i)); only the degree-one first root and the second isolated mark can give |J_i|=2k, and their total positive excess is at most (L_root+L_iso)/k.
claims.scope: Finite ordinary tree shell |T|=2p+2 with k=p-1 and one mark in each component of H_v; applies to each selected leaf without merging repeated supports.
claims.reason: A first-mark partition gives the exact identity, and the deletion/extension double count yields the asserted order-based sign and excess estimate. The edgeless H_v case is excluded by the shell eligibility guard.

limitations: The global selector-conditioned compensation inequality (Comp) remains unproved.
This route neither proves nor refutes the full first-order shell aggregate or the unrestricted lower-region aggregate.
No computational census or external theorem was used.
